utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Ms. Baen, you are continuing with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Baen: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bicic. Mr. Bicic --

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bicic, on Tuesday we ended the afternoon talking about your whereabouts the week of April 17th, 1992, and you said that you left town frequently for your business and also to move your family, because of the psychosis the week of April 17th, 1992. Let me ask you: You never left town, Bosanski Samac, for any other reason other than business and moving your family?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you said is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, you know Sulejman Tihic, do you not?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the president of the SDA in Bosanski Samac in April of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was the president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not sure whether he was the president of the SDA in Bosanski Samac in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was in the topmost leadership, according to what I heard, but whether he was president or not at that period, I'm not 100 per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Top leadership. Are you aware that he's already testified here in front of the Trial Chamber in this case?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever had any business dealings with Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of business dealings have you had with Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would often represent me. Actually, he was my attorney.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So other than in legal representation of you, did you have any other business dealings with Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have any dealings with the SDA itself? I know you said you weren't a member, but did you ever have any dealings with the SDA as far as assisting them in any way, or did you ever give any donations to the SDA, or did you ever contribute your services to the SDA in any way?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have an occasion to assist Mr. Tihic by transferring anything for him or the SDA?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never transferred any material for either Sulejman Tihic or the SDA on or about April 13th, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct; I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could I please ask your assistance in presenting these documents to the witness. And, Your Honour, may I ask the usher's assistance? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What are the documents? Can you --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They are entitled "Certificate," "SDA Certificate," dated April 13th, 1992. I have the original in the Bosnian version and there's a translation in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Has the Prosecution seen the documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we've seen this document. It was the one where I requested an investigator put it to my client. That's the document that was put by the investigator to the client after -- I said I -- I personally had no contact on this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. That's the document. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's the document. And I've -- as I've notified Defence, we will be objecting to its admission into evidence because there's -- we have no reason to believe it's authentic. But I think that will come out in the questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we just ask if the Court could please just mark it for identification purposes. That's all. And we understand the Prosecution's objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number for identification purposes only?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be D3/2 ter for the B/C/S and D3/2 for the English and ID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, do you have the Bosnian version of this exhibit in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read what is at the top left-hand corner of the document? Read out loud, please.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "SDA."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next two lines, please.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Party of Democratic Action. Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read the next two lines, including the date.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Number 36/92. Date: The 13th of April, 1992."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please read the title of the document in the middle of the page in bold type.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Certificate."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Bicic, could you please read for the Trial Chamber the next two paragraphs of the document.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It is certified that Hasan Bicic, son of Zijah, from Bosanski Samac, for the Party of Democratic Action needs, can transfer necessary materiel and equipment on the 13th of April, 1992. "This certificate is issued for the purpose of transferring materiel and technical equipment for SDA Bosanski Samac, and it cannot be used for any other purposes."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are the next two lines in this document on the lower right-hand corner underneath those two paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "President, Sulejman Tihic."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never were presented with this document by an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor earlier in the week?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't seen this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're telling me this week, Ms. Reidy or no investigator from the OTP ever showed you this document?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember ever having seen this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one more question. Let me just ask you one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe -- let's clear this. Maybe the copy isn't the one he saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I have no idea. This is exactly the one that we gave to the OTP, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has a copy which he actually saw?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The copy that -- well, the copy that I gave the investigator to -- to ask -- as I say, I wasn't -- I wasn't there. I don't know. Perhaps -- perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. But it was a photocopy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It was a photocopy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It's in my office at the moment, that actual copy that was shown, with some notes at the bottom from the investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that's all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm guessing it has to be probably a photocopy of the same -- of the same document, but, as I say, I don't know whether the investigator ever --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Showed him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- showed him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I asked him to ask three questions about the document and that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we've established, Mr. Bicic, that you've never seen this document before. Let me ask you one more question: You have told the Trial Chamber that you had never been a member of the SDA or assisted the SDA in any way. Do you have any idea why your name would appear on a SDA document of this kind?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Objection. Objection. We've simply said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: We've simply said that we would allow this document in for identification. Our whole purposes -- we have no way of proving that this is an SDA document. You can see -- well, perhaps -- there's no stamping, no signing. There's nothing to suggest there's any authenticity to this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- as indeed other documents have seen -- we've seen stamps on that. So to say that this is an SDA document is simply not a factual thing that's been proved. So why it appears on this form is another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because as it appears, like the Prosecution have said, you cannot conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: May I respond? We're going to certainly present this document to Mr. Tihic to see if he will authenticate it. Right now we're merely presenting this on cross-examination to see if this witness could identify it, which, number one, he can't. But if he can't, does he have any idea why this might even exist? I mean, we're allowed to cross-examine him on the document. We're not offering it for evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can, but not to make the conclusion that you're making and putting it to him as the Prosecution protested. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you may rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Bicic, I'm sure you're following what's going on. Mr. Tihic is coming back to cross-examine. We will ask him about this document. My question is: You're saying you've never seen this before. If Mr. Tihic says that this is an authentic document, do you have any idea why your name would appear on such a document?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a simple matter. Again, you're asking the witness to speculate on what Mr. Tihic might or might not say at any time in the future. The question, simply put to the witness, is: Do you know why your name is on this piece of paper? And the -- Ms. Baen is not allowed to attribute any other quality to this specific document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen. The objection is sustained. You can cross-examine without giving the impression to this witness that this document was authored by Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Tihic may not have authored this. It may be a totally bogus document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: But if it is authentic, which we won't have a chance to talk to Mr. Bicic about this again -- Mr. Tihic when he comes back and identifies this and says it's an authentic document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then that's a matter for closing arguments --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We're not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- because the witness has said he has never seen this document, and that is clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So you can't put it -- confuse him by trying to allege that this is -- this document was authored by Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: They're saying that it's not authentic. They're saying that it's a bogus document. So that's what I'm telling him. I'm saying the OTP has been saying that this is a bogus document, this is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where this will take you, but proceed, but provided that you bear in mind that the witness has said he has never seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: This is actually my last question, Your Honour. I just want him to answer that question, and then I'll sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm waiting for the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same question: Do you have any idea why your name is on this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, my name was on lots of different sorts of documents, signatures and everything that goes with that. So I hope that you're going to propose some of the ones that I signed in the Cyrillic alphabet when they beat me in the police station when I gave statements. I hope you have some of those documents too. As far as this is concerned, I mean this document, the one that is before me, I think that it would be even more credible or authentic in character if, in addition to the SDA and President Sulejman Tihic, there could have been the name of the president Alija Izetbegovic. It would be more credible then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer is you really have no idea why your name is on this document; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right; I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bicic. Your Honour, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The next counsel. Is it Mr. Lukic? Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours and all other participants in the courtroom. Before I start my cross-examination, I should like to ask the Court on this occasion to see the -- to introduce the English versions of the documents that I introduced when I examined Mr. Lukac on the 1st of October. In the meantime, I have received the official translation of the document and I have prepared the documents, and I think that this is the right time for me to tender them. They have been given ter numbers, D3 to D8 ter, and I would like to tender those documents into evidence. So I'd like to ask the usher's assistance. I have already handed in the documents to the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We can have the documents, and as they are already -- you have said they are official English translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They have been placed in order as they were introduced and as the documents were lined up in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we just have the formal numbering, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The English translations are numbered D3/3, D4/3, D5/3, D6/3, D7/3, and D8/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Just so we don't interrupt Mr. Lukic's cross, I'm not sure that we got all the official English translations. Or if he did, could you just tell me -- if it's just the one you gave to me, the single one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Four days ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. That's good. Then I'll follow that up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Four days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I wasn't clear. Is the Prosecution saying they haven't got the whole batch?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, it's okay. I just -- this morning Mr. Lukic gave me a document that he intended to tender into evidence, and the reference to the official English translations of previous documents, I just wanted to make clear if he had given it to our team members, because it wasn't me personally. But if he has already disclosed them, then it's a matter for the Prosecution to follow up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes, you can proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to clarify, I handed it to the Prosecution several days ago and I didn't want to tender it into evidence until this came up. But I can say that the Prosecution did receive copies of the official translation on the day that I received them too. That is certain. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bicic. My name is Attorney Novak Lukic and I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Miroslav Tadic, and on his behalf, I'm going to ask you several questions. First of all, Mr. Tadic has asked me to convey to you his regrets for everything that you experienced and recounted here before the Tribunal since the time you were arrested until the time you were released. But we are all here to clarify certain issues and facts, and we should like to ask for your assistance, as witness, to ascertain the relevant facts regarding the indictment and the trial that we are here about. I should like to move back quite a bit in time. You said that you were from an old Samac family. Was your father also a caterer, and was his name Zijah, the late Zijah?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he had a cafe. You said that you took over the family business of this cafe; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were a boy, you helped your father in that cafe serving customers, and that was one of the attractions, that your father would bring in his small son and dress you and that you would help him serve his customers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can say you were a caterer from the very earlier stage; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember that Mr. Miroslav Tadic used to frequent that old family cafe while you were still a boy, when your father was alive?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that you -- that he played cards with your father there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you were active with Mr. Tadic in the private entrepreneurs' association and that you were president of the catering association representing your particular branch.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you frequent the AS Cafe?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although I wasn't a very frequent guest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, from the beginning to the attack on the 17th of April, did you frequent it during that period?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you would stop by, were then the normal number of customers in the cafe? Was it frequented normally?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I suppose you know that people played cards there too.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was said that people would come to play cards there even from further afield, outside Samac, from Serbia and from Croatia. Would that be true?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm who came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure you know that there was a hall with a billiard table there and another one where cards were played.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know the fact that the cafe worked round the clock, as long as there were customers to sit in it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that. I know it was open for long hours. Whether it was actually non-stop, I can't say, but I know that it was open for long hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that some respected citizens would come to the cafe, these respected citizens of Samac who were not Serbs by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think everybody frequented that particular cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that members of all ethnic groups came to your pizza bar as well, regardless of national affiliation, ethnic affiliation.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think there were any ethnic bars or cafes in our town, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I completely agree with you there, and Mr. Todorovic's answer with respect to your arrest, with respect to the alleged meetings of the HDZ in your pizza parlour, as members of all ethnic groups would frequent the establishment, and that he was surprised that that was stated.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm glad we can agree on something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, would the same criteria hold true for the AS Cafe, that is to say that all ethnic groups frequented it, and if the cafe worked round the clock until there were any guests left present, and if people from outside Samac would come in for drinks and card playing?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the short time prior to the aggression on Samac - when I say "the short time," that is a debatable point - I don't know actually who came -- who went there, because I didn't go, but it was common knowledge that at least one month prior to the aggression, or even more than that, longer than that, different sorts of people would gather there. But who it was who actually frequented the establishment, I don't know, because I didn't go to the cafe at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you heard that members of the 4th Detachment frequented it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody in town knew that. Everybody knew that it was a meeting place or headquarters of some kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will agree with me that people understand meeting places and headquarters in different ways, they understand those terms differently?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that opposite the AS Cafe there was a shop -- the building of the SIT, Samac textile industry?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me now move on to a different area. Let me remind you of some of the answers you gave to the Prosecutor in answer to his questions. You said that after your arrest, that you were put up in the same room in SUP [redacted] with an elderly Albanian man, and with Sulejman Tihic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother was there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you all transferred to the warehouse of the Territorial Defence together?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that at this point in time. My brother and I were for sure, but with so much time gone by, I can't actually say whether we were all transferred at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in the TO warehouse, you were kept there for about ten days, after which you were transferred to Brcko; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, did you, during your incarceration in the TO warehouse, in that particular room, ever see Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And just one brief question, if you happen to remember: You recounted the events in detail with respect to Dikan's killing. Do you happen to remember in which vehicle, if it was a vehicle, was his body transferred and who the driver was of that vehicle, if it was indeed a vehicle and if you saw it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to move on to discuss what you said on one occasion when you had the -- received the happiest news, most joyous news, which was, in fact, news of your exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to introduce a list of exchange, the exchange list, which was used on the occasion when the witness was exchanged. It is the list which exists officially in the Prosecution's documents as evidence, and it was disclosed by the Defence in 1998 to the Prosecution, and before the start of trial, I sent this list to my colleagues of the Prosecution. I have a working translation, a draft translation, but a few days ago I gave the document up for official translation, which I haven't received yet. So can we tender this provisionally, the translation I have, while waiting for the official translation? It is the list, as I say, dating to 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we can have those documents, because when you give -- if the documents are going to be referred to the witness, obviously you have the Serbo-Croat, and then our interpreters can interpret whatever is written on them. Yes. So we can receive it. I just want to find out from the Prosecution if there's any objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: There's no -- no objection at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Before -- I'm sorry, before you ask, how many lists are you going to use? Only one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only one, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: B/C/S version will be numbered D12/3 ter and the English version D12/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to ask the usher to place the map, D15 - it is the Times map of Yugoslavia - on the ELMO, please. It is a large map.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm not sure it's a map that the Prosecution -- is it -- is it a large map that you're speaking -- I think Mr. Lukic is referring to the map that's mounted on a hard back back here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Then the usher would find it back here in the corner, rather than with the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bicic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The usher doesn't seem to be -- is there a map there? It's empty?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, you have before you a document which you might be seeing for the first time. It is a list. Can you just read the date and the heading, what it refers to?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the left? The title, or the list of persons exchanged, who left, on the 4th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That will be sufficient. Do you see your own name on the list? If so, could you tell us the number?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see my name under number ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that about ten people from your group left on that occasion. Do you recognise any of those people on this list of names? And please, if you happen to remember somebody, tell us.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll take it in order for persons whom I'm certain were from my group. As to the other names, I don't really know whether they were incarcerated in another prison or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So in addition to me under number ten, there was number 13, Atic Kemal. Next I think it was number 14, I think, Tolic Ilija. I think he was another one. Hurtic Salko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that number 25?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, number 25. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's as far as I can remember names. I allow for the possibility that there are others whom I could not identify by name now and who was in my group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Would you just read, next to number seven, the name Stipo Nogic. Can you tell us what it says here next to his name?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says he did not go in this exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read what it says under number 44, next to the name?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It just says "No."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you were exchanged on the 4th of July or sometime -- 4th of July or sometime around the 4th of July. Do you say it was on the 4th of July?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, on the big map of the former Yugoslavia, would you indicate Sid? I don't believe Lipovac is on the map, but if you could point to the town of Sid for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I should be able to find my way around. I have to stand up. I should stand up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness can stand up and look at the map closely if that will help.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found Sid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you move a little to the right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I wonder whether counsel can see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you indicate it once again and stand a little more to the side so that the Defence counsel can see?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Indicated on the map. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have no further questions related to the map, so the witness may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if it may be of assistance for the record and for the Trial Chamber to show -- just so the transcript records the fact that Mr. Bicic pointed with a pointer to a location which on the Times map is situated within Serbia. I mean, I think that's what we saw, and if perhaps the transcript could just reflect that. Would that be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I can't understand that --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- because he was asked to indicate where Sid is on the map. And what is your point?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: My point is that we could all see in this -- see in this room and see on the map that -- where he pointed to as being identified as Sid was located within the boundary of Serbia, and I was wondering whether it might be possible that the record could reflect that for future --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- reference if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is within the boundary of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yeah. And while we could all visibly see that from the map, it wouldn't be recorded as a -- on the transcript that we could cross-reference to in future if we needed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Okay. Yes. It will -- yes. It's already in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It's in the record. Okay. Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately how far away Lipovac is from Sid? After all this time, could you judge the distance?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't answer you with any precision, but it could be about 20 kilometres. I'm not sure about this though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that UNPROFOR mediated in your exchange. Are you familiar with the term UNPA zone, and if you are, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I heard about some terms such as the demarcation line later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that in the place of your exchange, there were representatives of the United Nations on the spot?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it perhaps the Russian battalion?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember there were representatives of the European Community there or OSCE?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see representatives of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only a few details in connection with the trip itself. Do you remember that you waited for a long time at the border between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, at a place called Raca where there is a bridge? Did the convoy halt there for a considerable period of time?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly where it was that we waited for a long time, but I do know that we waited for a few hours, and I heard that one of the buses had broken down. But where it was exactly that we waited and how long it was, I couldn't tell you now with any precision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that when the convoy set out from Samac, after a certain time it stopped in a wood near Bijeljina for people to take a rest and relieve themselves?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The witness never testified to any stop in the woods. If the -- of course the counsel wants to ask him whether he remembers any such a stop, that's one -- that's another matter. But I said -- he said-- he's suggesting in his question that the witness has testified to this being a fact, and in my recollection and my review of the transcript yesterday, I don't think the witness has ever testified to such a stop in the woods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. What you're saying is he shouldn't make a suggestion. He should just put the question straight to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm just simply saying he shouldn't infer that the witness has given that testimony himself. If he wants to ask whether it's true or not, of course he is entitled to, but not to imply that this is testimony the witness has given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure counsel has understood the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have understood the objection. I simply asked whether he remembered that the convoy stopped in the woods. I did not ask him whether he remembers testifying to this, but only whether he remembers it. I didn't say that he had said this here. That's in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. It's clear now. The witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember stopping in the woods or somewhere else, but I do remember that at several checkpoints we were stopped and that people wearing military uniform boarded the bus, threatened us. And I've already testified to this. They wanted to take one of the prisoners off the bus and so on. But where it was exactly, I couldn't recall now. No, I'm not able to recall it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the motel in Sid closed?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, I will ask you again whether you recall this: How many buses or vehicles were waiting for you on the other side, on the side under Croatian control, when you -- when you passed through the place where you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't be sure, but I know I was sitting in a bus. How many vehicles there were and what sort of vehicles they were, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there more than three buses?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer this with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the people who came to be exchanged from the other side when you were passing them by? Because the way I understood it, people passed by each other while they were being exchanged. That's what we saw on the video.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw some buses passing by, but I was not in any condition to -- I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's be very specific. Did you see on the other side that the people approaching towards your buses were elderly people, women, children? Were there people like this?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had been met by a friend who brought you some clothes and shoes.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was waiting for me at another motel near Zupanija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask him from whom he had found you out that you were to be exchanged, where he got this information?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember asking him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were released, I assume you tried to find out when your brother would be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's only natural. Yes, of course I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you apply to for information about when your brother would be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I applied to someone who had this information in Slavonski Brod while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of the commission for the exchange, the HVO commission for the exchange of prisoners and imprisoned civilians?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have heard of a Commission for Exchange. I think that's what its name was, something like that, the Commission for Exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brother, as far as I know, was exchanged in Dragalic in early September of the same year.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was about two months after your release?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have finished with the topic of exchanges. I will move on. I have just a few more questions. When did you first come back to Samac for the first time after July 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's another question I couldn't answer with any precision, but I can say perhaps -- well, yes. When I started working on this -- in connection with my property, the restoration of my property. So perhaps it was approximately a year and a half ago, but I can't be precise about the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, did the war in Samac begin on the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your view, did the war finish when the Dayton Accords were signed in 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't go into this now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the end of military operations, did you try to go back to Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have described the state in which you found your house when you went back to Samac. Do you know that your house was damaged by shelling, by shells coming from Croatian territory, in the course of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that for a time there was some sort of headquarters in my house. What kind of headquarters it was, I wouldn't know, whether it was military or police or what. I only heard that there was some sort of headquarters there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether you knew that the house had been destroyed by shelling.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what means was used to destroy it, but I allow for the possibility, because when I saw that the walls were damaged and the roof, I allow for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that a number of houses were damaged at the same time from shelling coming from HVO-controlled territory?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that other houses were damaged too, but I don't know where the shells came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Kenan Avdibegovic's house was damaged? He's a well-known figure.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the house was severely damaged, the house of the Repcic family, and that their child was a casualty?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On several occasions during this cross-examination, you said that from the moment of your arrest until your release, you made no decisions of your own free will.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said when Mr. Simic told you that you most probably would be exchanged, that this news filled you with joy and that you could hardly wait to tell this wonderful news to your brother.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the exchange, while you were waiting in the convoy, you said you were afraid that perhaps the exchange would not succeed.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question: Did you want to be exchanged; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The next counsel. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bicic. My name is attorney Pantelic and I am Defence counsel for Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will do my best not to speculate, like my colleague Ms. Baen did, but to go directly to the facts, and I won't force you to speculate, and so I hope that in this way we'll be able to stick to a 30-minute time limit. Mr. Bicic, let us ascertain some relevant categories essential for this trial. You were arrested on the 18th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were incarcerated in Samac at the SUP and the TO up until the end of April, which means around about the 27th or 28th of April?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were later transferred to Brcko, and I think that you were in Brcko until about the 1st of May.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Brcko, you were transferred to Bijeljina, and you were there until the middle of the month, so we can say until approximately the 15th of May; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can put it that way, although I don't know the precise date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That goes without saying, because a lot of time has gone by since then. But at all events, when you returned to Samac in mid-May, or rather, when you were returned, when they took you back, you spent two or three days in the secondary school building; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, sometime around the 20th of May, you were transferred to the primary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And practically speaking, you stayed in the primary school until the day of your exchange, which was sometime at the beginning of July or, rather, the 4th of July?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We've got through that time period and the details. Mr. Bicic, the members of paramilitary formations, on the morning of the 18th of April, asked money and other valuables of you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whose members they were, but what you say is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, those same members, in the SUP, forcibly took a gold chain that was around your neck away from you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, may we agree that Lugar seized your jeep from you and that you happened to recognise it, to notice it - at around the 20th of April, you saw him driving your jeep, in fact - and that there were a lot of goods from your pizzeria in it? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that I saw some of that up in the room when I was interrogated at the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let us take another route and say that we can agree on the fact that Lugar had seized your jeep; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My jeep was seized. Now, whether it was seized by Lugar or someone else, someone from his group, his team, I really can't say that now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did see Lugar driving your jeep; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In Brcko you were also searched, and they took away all your documents and valuables, the ones that you had managed to have with you still; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you also agree that while you were in Samac, you had contacts with somebody called Jusa and that he was from Belgrade? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that man, Jusa, had your gold chain on him; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he offered to return the chain to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I -- if Mr. Pantelic is suggesting that the witness has indeed said this, could he please, for the record and for our benefit as well, tell us when the witness is alleged to have said that he offered to return the chain to you? Because I'm not aware of that again being in the record. And if it's from another source, then I just think Mr. Pantelic should be putting on the record where he has that information from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think sometimes it's the problem of language, the way the questions are phrased. It's not necessarily that the witness did -- it is implied that the witness did give that evidence. It's clear to me that he's simply asking whether this particular man offered to return the chain to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In any case, I can withdraw this particular -- the last question, I can withdraw. It's no problem. Thank you so much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Bicic, may we agree that on that occasion, you had the impression that that man Jusa from Belgrade was some sort of superior in relation to the soldiers who seized the chain from you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, during this conversation with Jusa, did he say that he had a cafe in Belgrade and you had a cafe too, so that you were sort of colleagues along those cafe lines? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That we were colleagues, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I mean as caterers, owners of cafes.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that he had been to my house. He first of all asked me whether I recognised the chain. I said I recognised it but that I was no longer interested in it, and then he said that allegedly he would save it for me and would return it to me after the war. And he gave me a carton of cigarettes, and yes, he said that he had been to my house and that allegedly he had leafed through some photographs and saw that I had a daughter and he himself had a daughter and a catering establishment in Belgrade and that I reminded him of himself and that we even used the same aftershave lotion. So he apologised and said he had taken a bottle of that aftershave lotion or perfume, whatever, and then he discreetly asked me whether I wished him to make some documents for me, compile some documents for me which would allow me and my brother to get out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You have come to my next question, actually, anticipated it. This man Jusa offered to make false documents for you and your brother and to transfer you both across Serbia into Hungary, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May I clarify with the witness? What year was this and month, if possible, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you answer Her Honour?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992. It was when I was incarcerated in the primary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, on that occasion, this man Jusa wanted you to drive your new Mercedes off as well once he had made up these documents for you and allowed you to go off into Hungary?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that he thought it was hidden somewhere, in somebody's garage perhaps or something of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it was your impression that he was using this as bait in order to learn where your Mercedes was and to seize the Mercedes from you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't believe anything to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You will agree with me when I say that it was your impression at that time that the beatings in the TO were for economic reasons actually, is that right, lucrative reasons?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A certain person called Lazo Troja asked 30.000 German marks from -- of you, along with the obligation to talk to the competent authorities and to pull you out of your incarceration; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, I am very kindly requesting that you now read part of your statement given in your own language for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And may I ask for the usher's assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the statement you gave to the Prosecutor, I think dated the 7th of March 1998. Can you read the portion -- that is to say, the last paragraph, which begins with "I think"? Read slowly for the interpreters, please. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Could Mr. Pantelic identify where in the English statement we should be looking at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. So you want --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would happily do that, but unfortunately, I have a very awful and bad copies of English. So probably the copy machine in Prosecution office was so exhausted. So I have only B/C/S, unfortunately, as I said. I mean, I followed it standard, but I really cannot make any reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we found it. If it helps the Chamber, I think it's -- sorry. You don't have copies of the statement. Then I think we've found it for the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the counsel asked the witness to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [As read] "I think that all the beatings at the TO also had an economic purpose. I ask not see it then, but I've been thinking about it after I was released. After almost every beating, a Serb called Lazo, a.k.a. Trajan," with an "N" - it says "Troja" here, but he's "Trojan" with an "N" - "from Slatine turned up. He brought us pills and asked what had happened to poor you. He asked us for money to save us. He told us that he could pay JNA officers to release us. He can have been the man who organised the beatings - I'm thinking about myself - to get money. Before the war, I think he was a criminal. He was a criminal before the war." That's what it says in the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Verbatim; Interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you turn to the next page, please?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [As read] "Sulejman Tihic, with the help of people, gave him more than 20.000 Deutschemarks by help from people outside the camp but was not released." Do you want me to go on reading?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "After I had been severely beaten, Lazo also started the game with me. He said that if I could, that he would get -- if I could give him 30.000 Deutschemarks, he would get me and my brother out of the country. I told him that I had not money in Bosanski Samac but I had in Hungary. Lazo said that he could not deal this way, because he first had to give the money to Serbian officers. Lazo did never join the beating, but I have reason to believe that many detainees were beaten because of him. It was their way of earning money."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one correction. You said -- [In English] in the transcript we have the word "but I had in Hungary," which is not true. Actually, the witness followed the statement, and it was --

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's left out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's left out. It's not "Hungary." It's just left out. Probably due to the confidential matters in English version this name of this place was struck out. So it wasn't actually -- while reading, he didn't mention a fact that he got money in Hungary, in Hungary. Just for a clarification.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. I said that I was -- that I was able to pay once he had transferred me to Hungary. I didn't say that I had money actually in Hungary, but perhaps that's not important at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bicic. Having read out the statement that you gave in 1998, can we agree that you had the strong impression that the basis for all that mistreatment was the seizing and looting of money, cars, gold chains, foreign currency by those bandits actually; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, I could agree with you. At the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That was the beginning, and you're probably coming to another point now. Could you clarify what you mean by what you've just said?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can clarify it by saying that after they had seized all the valuables, after everything had been looted and plundered, the beatings continued to be very strong, and all the abuse as well. So they had nothing more to seize, but they went on beating, just -- why? You would have to ask them that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, that is my impression too. Mr. Bicic, we can agree with the fact, can we not, that apart from Stiv Todorovic being the chief of police, that he was -- that he beat you strongest with some sort of baseball bats and bars; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is my impression, on the basis your statements and these general proceedings, that that man, Stevan Todorovic, took it out on you particularly because he wanted to date your girlfriend who had rejected him, the girl from Orasje, I believe.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that afterwards, after my imprisonment. She never mentioned that, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your impression, when you learned about all this, was that he took it out on you in particular precisely because, let us say, that sentimental -- those sentimental reasons, if I can put it that way; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, among other things. Probably because of that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once again talking about Stevan Todorovic, during the beatings he would laugh like a maniac. That is what you said in your very words, and I suppose you stand by them.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can state here and now that he took pleasure in ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers. Mr. Bicic, when you were in the secondary school building, you said that Blagoje Simic turned up and entered the hall, took a look around, made no comment, and left, went out. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, accompanied by Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anybody else along with Blagoje Simic and Stevan Todorovic? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the two of them alone?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, but I knew the two of them, so I can say that the two of them were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about in that hall with you? Who was there? Could you enumerate all the people who were in the hall with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly they were all the people from the group who they had returned from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us a few names, please?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother, Ibrahim Salkic, Mersad Gibic. I can't now remember all the names, but for the most part almost the whole group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you this, because I have consulted my client and he says that he was never there, which means that you are lying; right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You're lying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think counsel provoked that sort of answer from the witness by suggesting to him. He could be mistaken, for instance, but he has given us the answer. But, Witness, don't be rude to the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, tell me, please, were you a member of some sort of local party-armed formation; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of a party-armed formation in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have two documents here. Mr. Usher, I would like your assistance. There is enough copy for Trial Chamber, for Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The documents are actually part of the previously admitted documents of the military headquarter of SDA party in Samac and Crisis Staff in Samac. These two documents, namely attachment number 6 and attachment number 8, are related. Attachment number 6 is the communications section, which has the same form as the previous that I mentioned, and attachment number 8 is the Hunters' section, just for the -- to facilitate your following. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution -- has the Prosecution seen the documents or --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we haven't. As I said, the other counsel did indicate which documents they wanted to use. I understand from Mr. Pantelic's answers he said that they are part of documents that he said are already in evidence. Then they should have an exhibit number. If that's the case, then of course we have them. Apart from that, we've never been given any other document from Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I have to be clear what he says, they are part of the documents. I don't know what that means. They could be in a similar classification but certainly different documents, in which case they would have different numbers if they were to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Well, he hasn't indicated if they have an exhibit number, so I don't know. And apart -- as I said, apart from exhibits that have already been entered into evidence, Mr. Pantelic has not provided us with any documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify that, Madam President. I mean, this document was disclosed to the Prosecution in pre-trial phase by my colleague Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So it hasn't got a number on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: They're in possession of this document. And you will see at the first moment that are the same document that we have discussed about the military Crisis Staff of SDA party and the headquarter in Samac. Just a couple of questions, and we shall finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What I want to be clear about is this: This document that you want to discuss with the witness, has it been discussed already or is it similar to other documents discussed? In which case it is a new document, and we have to give it a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have to give it a number. I want to tender it in evidence, because this is a part of my cross-examination and it's a completely new document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For the references, for the facilitation, I make these notes. So I kindly ask to have a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- pending Prosecution examination of this document and that -- if it could be only given an identification number, because the Prosecution would object to its initial admission into evidence until we have some time to consider the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree. I agree with that. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we can have the numbers for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Numbers for identification will be number D16/1 ter for attachment number 6 for the B/C/S version and D16/1 for the English; attachment number 8 will be D17/1 ter for the B/C/S and D17/1 for the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, could you turn the page of the document you have before you and read out the Bosnian version of the document on the right-hand side. What does it say? Attachment --

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Attachment 6."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the title of the document?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Communication Section."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Under number 4, would you read out the name, please.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hasan Bicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the number following it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that you? That is you. And is that your telephone number?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is my home telephone number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bicic, open the next document, please. Turn to -- turn the page, please, because that is the English version, and read out the upper right-hand corner. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Attachment 8."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the title of the document?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Hunters' Section."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 1, where it says "reserve," what is the name?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muhamed Bicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your brother?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muhamed Bicic is my brother, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the telephone number? Is that his telephone number?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is, his home number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] I think we are now 11.00. So we can take a break, Your Honour, if you agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break and start again at 1130 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic continuing cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bicic, you have had a look at the documents. You did so before we had our break. Can you confirm that you were a member of the communications section within the armed formation of the SDA party in Bosanski Samac; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge about the fact that your mother was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your brother, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- was in the reserve formation for the Hunters' within the framework of the SDA party formation in Bosanski Samac; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, may we agree that just one number of -- just a part of the population of Samac of Muslim ethnicity and Croatian ethnicity, after the 17th of April, was arrested; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was incarcerated. I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You were incarcerated with some other Muslims and Croats from Bosanski Samac; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that not all Muslims or all Croats from Bosanski Samac were incarcerated in Bosanski Samac under the control of the Serb police force and paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place I was in, the area I was in, was not sufficient to take everybody in, was not big enough for everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but did you know at the time that only a portion of the population, on some grounds, whatever grounds, legal or illegal, were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that, for the most part, those people were Muslims and Croats within the framework of party and certain armed formations; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your incarceration, did anyone in the police force or in the TO tell you why you were under detention?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the reason they gave?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They mentioned certain lists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bicic, can you confirm the fact that during your education, both the Latin and Cyrillic scripts were equally used, used on an equal footing at school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how much they were equally used, but we were taught both, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm asking you. So you can read and write in Cyrillic, can you not?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I use the Latin script myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but I assume that during your years at school you had to write certain things in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used the Cyrillic script only when I had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's just what I wanted to hear from you, what I was asking. Thank you. One more question, and that completes my cross-examination. Mr. Bicic, I'm now going to, with the usher's assistance, show you part of your statement to read. It is the statement you gave to the Prosecution on the 7th of March, 1998 and it is in your mother tongue. Just one sentence, and the sentence has been marked in black. Would you please read out that sentence.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can do --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I can just make a reference that the B/C/S version is number 00637131, and that is the, well, fourth paragraph. But actually, I don't know. Is it -- relates to English version, because the kind of typing is different, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
